Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THIS IS A TEMPURA HOUSE AND THERE IS NOTHING HERE FOR A COELIAC ON THE MAIN BOARD — every tendon and every tempura plate is wheat batter, and the tare poured over a Daikokuya tendon is soy, mirin and sugar. That is said plainly rather than worked around. ⚠ WHAT IS WORTH RECORDING IS THE SIDE BOARD, because an old Asakusa tempura shop keeps a proper 一品 list and several of those plates have no flour in them at all: さしみ ¥2,400, あじのたたき ¥900, 胡瓜もみ ¥700, おろし和え ¥700 and なめたけおろし和え ¥500 are constructed without batter. All are eaten with soy sauce, which is where the wheat sits, and all but the cucumber are fish. 茄子のしぎやき at ¥800 is aubergine in miso — the one plate here that is plant in substance. ⚠ AND ONE PORTION NOTE THAT MATTERS FOR A GROUP: 御飯 is ¥250 and お吸物 ¥350, so a person who cannot eat tempura can sit down to rice, soup and pickles for well under ¥1,000 while the table has tendon. The soup is a dashi, so it is bonito.

tokyo_shochiku_en_cafe.price_note: ⚠ A CAFÉ WHERE THE ENTIRE MENU CLEARS BOTH DIETS, WHICH HAS NOT HAPPENED BEFORE IN THIS DATASET. 松竹圓カフェ brands itself Vegan & Gluten-free Cafe and repeats the claim under every section in the same two sentences: 「全てのメニューはオリエンタルビーガン対応（動物由来の食材及び五葷不使用）になっております」 and 「全てのメニューは、グルテンフリー(小麦不使用)となっております」. So: no animal ingredient, no 五葷 (garlic, spring onion, onion, nira, rakkyo — the Buddhist 精進 exclusion, which goes beyond veganism), and no wheat, across cakes, pizza and drinks alike. It adds 「ビーガンの方や卵、乳製品、小麦アレルギーの方も安心してお召し上がり頂けます」, naming egg, dairy and WHEAT ALLERGY explicitly. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THE PIZZA IS THE HEADLINE: 「米粉の生地のカリッともっちりした美味しさ」 — a RICE FLOUR base, made in-house, with a 五葷-free tomato sauce. A gluten-free pizza is close to unobtainable in Tokyo and this one is also vegan, including a plant ベーコン. Sold by the slice at ¥350–380 and as whole pies at ¥2,800–3,040. ⚠ AND THE CAKES USE A GF SPONGE: the tiramisu is described as 手作りの豆乳チーズ over a コーヒーベースのGFスポンジ — soy-milk cheese on a gluten-free sponge. The rainbow cake, the shop’s 看板メニュー, is coloured 1枚1枚お野菜の色味をつけて — with vegetables rather than dye. ⚠ WHAT IS STILL WORTH ASKING, and this record does not claim otherwise: the shop states its recipes, not its supply chain. It publishes no statement about factory cross-contamination in bought-in ingredients the way まるごとVeganダイニング浅草 does, and it does not describe a separated kitchen. The flags below are set to the shop’s own declaration because it is explicit, first-party and repeated — but a coeliac should still ask about shared equipment, which is the one question the page does not answer. ⚠ AND THE DRINKS CARRY SOMETHING RARE: plant milks are an explicit paid option — 無調整豆乳, アーモンドミルク and オーツミルク at +¥100 each. Almost no other café in this dataset lists one at all.

tokyo_soul_food_india_suido_ba.price_note: The shop publishes a full priced card across four pages and states 「※ここで掲載するメニューの価格はすべて税込表記になります」 — all prices tax-included. ⚠ ONE DISCREPANCY ON THE SHOP'S OWN PAGE, RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED OVER: the dinner page renders its おつまみ block twice (desktop and mobile layouts) and three items carry different prices in the two blocks — ほかほか焼き枝豆 appears at both ￥490 and ￥390, きのこのバター醤油風味 at both ￥490 and ￥390, and インドの焼きそば チョーミン at both ￥920 and ￥900. The higher figure of each pair is recorded below with the alternative noted; check in the shop. ⚠ WHY AN INDIAN KITCHEN IS THE BEST NEWS IN THIS WHOLE SHARD FOR A COELIAC, AND EXACTLY WHERE IT STOPS. Indian curry is thickened with onion, tomato, nuts and cream rather than a wheat roux, which makes it structurally unlike Japanese curry — and this shop lets you take every single curry with RICE instead of naan, including at lunch where it prints ライス大盛無料. That one substitution converts most of the card. The wheat is concentrated almost entirely in the bread: プレーンナン, ごまナン, ガーリックナン, チーズナン and ガーリックチーズナン are all wheat, and ロティ is explicitly 全粒粉, wholemeal — wholemeal is still wheat, and the word 全粒粉 on a menu misleads people constantly. ⚠ THE TWO GENUINELY PROMISING SIDES, AND THE FRYER PROBLEM THAT SITS UNDER BOTH. パパド at ￥390 is a lentil-flour chip and パコラ at ￥690 is a chickpea-batter fritter — both are naturally wheat-free forms, and they are the sort of thing a coeliac almost never gets offered in Japan. They are recorded ask, not gf, for two reasons: commercial papad is sometimes cut with wheat flour or asafoetida compounded with wheat, and both are deep-fried in oil this kitchen also uses for サモサ, whose pastry is wheat. Ask about the fryer. ⚠ THE VEGAN PICTURE IS BETTER THAN USUAL AND STILL NEEDS ONE QUESTION. ベジタブルカリー at ￥1200 is a permanent plant curry, and パコラ, ポテトのホットスパイシー炒め, スパイシーインディアントマトサラダ and 緑トマトのさっぱり漬け are all plant dishes. The question to ask is ghee and cream: North Indian kitchens routinely finish vegetable curries with butter or dairy cream, and バターチキン and チキン コルマ on the same card show this kitchen works in that idiom. ライタ is explicitly yoghurt and サグ is usually creamed. ⚠ AND ONE ITEM THAT LOOKS INDIAN AND IS NOT: インドの焼きそば チョーミン is chow mein — wheat noodles, plus a soy-based stir-fry seasoning. きのこのバター醤油風味 names 醤油 outright.
